correctness.rationale: On A⊕B⊕C an equivalence class meeting A and B absorbs all A by downward confluence; one meeting B and C absorbs all C by upward confluence. A class meeting A and C absorbs B and is universal. If the lower mixed class L exists, any middle world outside it must belong to an upper mixed class H (use upward confluence at its middle target); the dual follows from downward confluence. Thus exactly five mutually exclusive types are possible. Each admits literal witnesses to both conditions, including equal-world, singleton-level, and universal boundaries. Disjoint class enumeration gives Bell(a)Bell(b)Bell(c)+Bell(a)+Bell(c)+2^b−1 for all positive a,b,c. The standalone checker independently exhausts all 102,487 labelled partitions across 56 size triples of total size three through eight, compares both quantified laws with the five-type criterion for every partition and validates all individual counts; it returns ALL_CHECKS_OK. Finite enumeration corroborates but does not replace the symbolic proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete structural classification of a natural combination of S5 epistemic equivalence and both constructive modal persistence conditions. Three antichain levels provide the first internal branching layer where two disjoint opposite-direction cross-level classes are possible. The proof shows this exhausts all nonuniversal cross-level shapes, yielding an exact three-parameter Bell-number census rather than a routine small case or arbitrary invariant. It gives an explicit finite frame search-space reduction and clarifies the difference between ordinary confluence witnesses and strict triangle closure. No general modal completeness or downstream consequence is claimed.
